figures.title: Information production can outgrow human inspection
figures.caption: Information production can outgrow human inspection; governed decision context preserves what could change a decision.
figures.alt: A wide band of growing records, events, findings and model interpretations narrows through a governed decision context into one accountable Decision Owner with finite attention.
figures.description: A funnel with three stages. At the top, a wide band: information production keeps growing, as records, events, deterministic findings, analytical results and model interpretations. In the middle, the governed decision context, which keeps what could change a decision and shows its source, scope, gaps and owner. At the bottom, the Decision Owner, who has finite attention and is accountable. The step from the wide band to the context is labeled authorize, select, label; the step from the context to the owner is labelled one decision packet.

figures.title: Reference architecture
figures.caption: Nine steps on the main path lead to one review contract; mandatory continuity and execution authority retain separate, governed paths.
figures.alt: A main path of nine numbered steps from sources to review of one decision packet, with a separate mandatory continuity path, a separate action path, a reassessment and invalidation loop, and a control plane that constrains every stage.
figures.description: The main path, on the left, has nine steps: sources, admission, the registry of immutable versions (C02), authorized retrieval (C01), relevance and coverage, the selection manifest (C03), bounded synthesis, release validation, and review of the decision packet (C04) by the Decision Owner. A separate mandatory continuity path leaves the registry and runs through deterministic detection and an authorized notification queue to acknowledgement or escalation; acknowledgement is receipt, not resolution, and the path has no LLM dependency. A separate action path starts from the review step: an exact approved proposal (C05) or bounded grant (C06) reaches an executor that performs current checks, then an authoritative target, then a verified receipt (C07). The outcome returns to a reassessment and invalidation step, which also receives corrections, revocations, late evidence and challenges, and returns to the registry. A control plane constrains every stage and path: identity, authorization, purpose, domain policy, inventory, freshness, budgets and delegation.

figures.title: Common-source agreement is not corroboration
figures.caption: Common-source agreement is not corroboration; conflicts, corrections and the scope of validation stay visible.
figures.alt: Source record S01 version 1 is the single parent of model inferences M01 and M02, which both feed decision packet P01. Dashed arrows show typed relationships that are not ancestry: S02 contradicts S01, S01 version 2 supersedes S01 version 1 and invalidates M01 and M02, and V01 validates S01 version 1 only.
figures.description: Solid arrows are derivation ancestry. Source record S01/v1 is the only parent of two model inferences, M01/v1 from Agent A and M02/v1 from Agent B, which together form one origin. Both feed the decision packet P01/v1. A conflicting source record, S02/v1, also reaches the packet, so the conflict stays visible. Dashed arrows are typed relationships, not ancestry, and each names the actor who asserted it: S02/v1 contradicts S01/v1; a correction, S01/v2, supersedes S01/v1 and invalidates what was derived from it; and a scoped validation, V01/v1, assesses S01/v1 only. In the worked example, S01 is the goods receipt, S02 the invoice, and M01 and M02 the two model summaries.

figures.title: Anatomy of a decision packet
figures.caption: A decision packet makes evidence consumable while exposing interpretation, gaps, obligations and unexecuted proposals to an accountable owner.
figures.alt: The Decision Owner reviews a decision packet made of eight groups, G02 to G09. Claims, inferences and conflicts point to evidence records; coverage and obligations point to the selection manifest; action proposals point to action proposal records.
figures.description: The Decision Owner reviews one decision packet (C04), bound to an exact context, selection and as-of time (group G01). The packet has eight further groups: G02 supported claims, each citing an exact record version; G03 labeled inferences, with method and limits, never claims; G04 recommendations, with the accountable review requirement; G05 conflicts and uncertainty, visible and never settled by majority; G06 coverage, omissions and gaps, with seven missingness labels; G07 obligations, priority and mandatory items; G08 action proposals, proposed and not executed; and G09 review and version history. Claims, inferences and conflicts point to evidence records (C02) by exact version, claim or payload pointer and original locator. Coverage and obligations come from the selection manifest (C03). Action proposals point to action proposal records (C05).

figures.title: From proposal to commit
figures.caption: Current read permission, accountable approval and execution checks are separate; shared grant capacity and authoritative outcomes bound action.
figures.alt: A sequence from a packet listing a proposal, through approval of the exact proposal or a standing class grant, to the gateway's recheck at commit, reservation of allowance, submission to the target, a receipt, and authoritative verification. If any check fails, the receipt records a not-executed outcome with the reasons.
figures.description: Five participants: the Decision Owner, the approver or grant issuer, the gateway and executor, the target system and the receipt (C07). The packet lists a proposal as proposed, not executed. The Decision Owner asks the approver to approve this exact proposal version, or a standing class grant already covers it; the approval or grant (C06) names scope, limits and expiry. Approval is not commit: at commit the gateway rechecks that the grant is current and not revoked, the evidence is current and fresh, the preconditions hold, the parameters and target are permitted, and the per-action and cumulative limits hold, counting consumed plus reserved capacity. If every check passes, it reserves allowance, submits the exact action to the target, receives an outcome or a timeout and records a receipt: completed, unknown or partial. If any check fails, it records a receipt that says not executed, with the reasons. An authoritative verifier then confirms or reconciles the outcome.

figures.title: Receipt states and recovery
figures.caption: An unknown outcome keeps its reservation: only authoritative reconciliation settles it, and a timeout never restores allowance.
figures.alt: A submitted action becomes unknown or partial (amber, unresolved) or completed_verified or not_executed_verified (green, terminal). Unknown becomes completed or not executed, and partial becomes completed, only through reconciliation.
figures.description: An action starts as submitted, after the gateway has passed every check and reserved allowance. It leads to four states. Unknown (a timeout or no response) and partial (some effects verified, others not; known effects stay charged) are unresolved: allowance stays reserved or charged, there is no blind retry, and a timeout or lease expiry never restores allowance. Completed_verified (an authoritative outcome confirms the effect) and not_executed_verified (authoritatively verified: no business effect) are terminal. Unknown leaves only by authoritative reconciliation, to completed_verified or not_executed_verified. Partial leaves by reconciliation or compensation under policy, to completed_verified. Allowance is restored only on authoritative reconciliation, never by assuming that silence means no effect.

figures.title: Degraded information, closed execution
figures.caption: Information limitations are explicit, while invalid authority blocks execution in every state; urgent continuity uses its own authorized route.
figures.alt: A table with four rows of information state and four columns: what the reader sees, review, execution with valid current authority, and execution with invalid or uncertain authority. Execution is closed in the last column in every row.
figures.description: Information availability and authority validity are separate axes. The table lists four information states and, for each, what the reader sees, what review is possible, and whether execution is open when authority is valid and current or closed when authority is invalid or uncertain. Execution is closed whenever authority is invalid or uncertain, even when information is available and the recommendation sounds compelling. Urgent continuity runs on its own channel in every row.

rows: Qualified: stale, partial, or a source unavailable
The packet with labeled gaps; never a clean negative
Eligible only if the action's own evidence and precondition checks still pass
A qualified deterministic template, or a native or manual route; unsupported synthesis is not released as advice
Authorization or revocation cannot be established
Blocked for what depends on it
table.footnote: In every row, urgent continuity (independent deterministic notification, queue, acknowledgement and escalation) uses its own authorized channel. If that channel fails, the failure is exposed and the approved continuity or escalation route is followed.

figures.title: Complexity must earn its place
figures.caption: Complexity must earn its place against matched native, deterministic and zero-specialist baselines; no evaluation result is claimed.
figures.alt: Four steps in order: native or current workflow, deterministic grouping and templates, simple synthesis with zero specialists, optional specialists. Each step is compared with the one before on matched tasks. A note lists the measures and says every comparison is not run.
figures.description: Four steps, each compared with the one before on matched tasks, risks, scope and acceptance criteria. First the native or current workflow; then deterministic grouping and templates; then simple synthesis with zero specialists, which is a complete architecture on its own; and only then optional specialists, admitted only for a documented task, permission or isolation need that has been measured on a matched comparison. The measures are correctness, omissions, evidence actually inspected, decision quality, time and workload: not fluency, and not how many agents agree. No evaluation result is claimed; every comparison is not run.

figures.title: Which missingness label applies?
figures.caption: Seven labels, six questions, asked in order: an expected input that is not in front of the reader gets exactly one label.
figures.alt: A decision tree. A stale record gives stale. Otherwise a check not performed gives not_assessed, a principal not permitted gives inaccessible, no answer from the source gives unavailable, no completed scoped retrieval gives missing, an observed absence with method, time and complete coverage gives negative, and otherwise not_retrieved.
figures.description: For an expected input that is not in front of the reader, ask six questions in order. One: is a record available but failing the freshness requirement? If yes, the label is stale. Two: was the check or assessment performed? If not, not_assessed. Three: may the reader's principal read the source? If not, inaccessible, and the reason and existence are disclosed only when permitted. Four: did the source or dependency answer? If not, unavailable, which is not the same as denied. Five: did a scoped retrieval complete? If not, missing: expected, not obtained, reason may be unknown. Six: was absence observed with method, time and complete coverage? If yes, negative. If not, not_retrieved: a completed retrieval found nothing, which is not evidence of absence.

figures.title: A late correction reaches a pending approval
figures.caption: A late correction reaches a pending approval: derivatives and approvals stop being current, and the queued action is refused at commit.
figures.alt: A sequence in which a correction is admitted, supersedes the earlier record and invalidates what was derived from it; the packet is invalidated, a revised packet is produced and the pending approval is revoked; the queued action is then refused at the gateway and a not-executed receipt records why.
figures.description: Five participants: the source owner, the evidence registry (C02), the lineage service, the packets (C04) and approvals (C06), and the gateway. An approval is already queued for a later run. The source owner admits a correction as a new version. The registry records that it supersedes the earlier version. The lineage service invalidates the findings and summaries derived from it, then invalidates the packet that rested on them. A revised packet is produced with its prior version linked, and the pending approval is revoked. When the queued action reaches commit, the gateway rechecks and finds the grant revoked and the evidence no longer current; it refuses, and the receipt (C07) records not executed, with the reasons. A new proposal on the revised packet needs a new approval.

figures.title: How the seven contracts refer to each other
figures.caption: Context, selection, packet, proposal, delegation and receipt chain forward; evidence is referenced by exact version from the others.
figures.alt: Contracts C01 context, C03 selection, C04 decision packet, C05 action proposal, C06 delegation and C07 execution receipt chain downward, each referencing the ones before it. C02 evidence is referenced by exact version from C03, C04, C05, C06 and C07 with dotted lines.
figures.description: C01 context is referenced by C03 selection. C03 is referenced by C04 decision packet, together with the context. C04 is referenced by C05 action proposal, together with the context. A C06 delegation is bound to an exact C05 proposal or to a bounded class. A C07 execution receipt references one proposal and one grant. C02 evidence records are referenced, by exact version, claim or pointer, from the selection, the packet, the proposal, the delegation and the receipt; these references are drawn dotted.

banner.title: Evidence at Human Scale
banner.alt: Evidence at Human Scale. Systems produce evidence, AI makes it consumable, people remain accountable. Evidence is not inference, not recommendation, not authority.
